characters.id: dc:Wonder Woman|Golden Eagle Armor Wonder Woman
characters.continuity: DC Comics (Post-Crisis, New Earth, and modern comic appearances)
characters.summary: Wonder Woman donning the mythical golden eagle armor, a heavily armored, winged battle array designed for cosmic or apocalyptic threats. The armor provides enhanced protection and grants the wearer sustained flight capabilities.

techniques: Amazon close combat while fully armored (the armor marks a serious, all-out fight)

mechanisms: Heavy golden body armor providing advanced impact and energy resistance
Full-body golden armor and eagle helmet worn over her usual kit; she put it on while injured during the Devastation arc
Bullet-deflecting bracelets and reflexes, which normally provide most of her protection

weaknesses: Restricted agility compared to her standard unarmored state due to bulk and wings

depictions.title: DC Comics Post-Crisis (New Earth) / Wonder Woman Vol 2: the golden eagle armor as worn in the Devastation arc (1999) and Our Worlds at War (2001); the design originates in the Elseworlds Kingdom Come (1996), which is a separate continuity

limitations: Typically reserved only for catastrophic or universe-threatening battles due to its symbolic and heavy nature
Armor is equipment she dons only for serious fights; it is not a permanent form and its protective limits are not documented in the sources
characters.formDifferences: Adds heavy metallic protection, a winged helmet, and active mechanical or mystical wings for flight, trading some standard speed and agility for massive durability.

characters.earlierSummary: Post-Crisis Diana in the winged golden eagle armor, a full suit with eagle helmet that she dons only for especially serious fights. In Wonder Woman Vol 2 she wore it while injured in the 1999 Devastation arc and against the universe-destroying Imperiex in Our Worlds at War (2001). Her flight, speed and strength remain her own Hermes- and god-granted powers; the sources do not credit the armor's wings with flight.

characters.continuity: DC Comics (DC Rebirth, Justice League Dark, and Witching Hour crossover event)
characters.summary: Wonder Woman infused with the powerful magic of Hecate as one of the Witchmarked. In this form, she channels immense mystical energy capable of banishing elder demons and manipulating magical fabric.

techniques: Hecate-mark magic strong enough to banish the Upside-Down Man

mechanisms: Divinely reinforced durability amplified by Hecate's mark
Not established by the cited sources (no magical shield or boosted invulnerability is described for this form)

weaknesses: Vulnerability to corrupting higher-tier magical entities who claim ownership of the mark
The Witchmark is a channel for Hecate: the goddess possessed Diana fully at Nanda Parbat, and Zatanna and Constantine's exorcism went wrong
Circe trapped her in the Collective Unconscious and took control of her body during the Witching War

depictions.title: DC Rebirth (Prime Earth): Justice League Dark Vol 2 'Last Age of Magic' and the 2018 'The Witching Hour' crossover with Wonder Woman Vol 5 (#56-57), followed by 'The Witching War'

limitations: Magic is tied to Hecate's influence and can risk psychological or spiritual possession if over-channeled
The magic is a fraction of Hecate's power stored in her Witchmark: dormant until the Upside-Down Man activated it, and lost after Hecate's defeat when Circe absorbed the Witchmarked's power
Banished the Upside-Down Man only with Zatanna's guidance
characters.formDifferences: Replaces standard physical/Amazonian combat reliance with immense raw magical projection, sigil casting, and direct manipulation of mystical entities.

characters.earlierSummary: Diana as the most powerful of Hecate's Witchmarked. Marked by Hecate as a child, she carried a fraction of the goddess's magic, which lay dormant until the Upside-Down Man activated it. With it she banished that demon; Hecate later possessed her, but Diana retook her body, opened a portal for the Upside-Down Man to devour Hecate, restored the Sphere of the Gods and lost the magic.

characters.summary: Zatanna Zatara is a powerful Homo magi stage magician and premier spellcaster. She casts formidable arcane spells instantaneously by speaking words backwards, granting her control over reality, elements, and mental states.

techniques: Spells written in her own blood when she cannot speak

mechanisms: Healing spells: closed a gunshot wound to her own throat with a blood-written spell (Detective Comics #833)

weaknesses: Inability to cast spells if rendered mute or physically prevented from speaking or writing backwards
Vulnerability to physical surprise attacks before a defensive spell can be verbalized
Gagging her or restraining her mouth has incapacitated her
Can be ambushed physically before she casts: the disguised Joker shot her in the throat (Detective Comics #833)

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics New Earth Hunter Zolomon as Zoom (Flash vol. 2 #197, 2003). Excludes Prime Earth, TV and other versions; Prime Earth details differ.
characters.summary: Wally West's rival, whose chronokinesis lets him change how fast time runs around him rather than drawing on the Speed Force. He was unraveled by Wally's own time manipulation.

techniques: alters the speed time flows relative to himself
speed-based attacks as a consequence of that power
offense.range: close; extends to wherever his local time field reaches (not sourced)

mechanisms: local time manipulation used evasively (inferred from power description)

notableResults.citation: Flash comics summarised on DC Database and Wikipedia mirror
notableResults.note: Wally turned time-stream manipulation against him, unraveling Zoom's timeline and reverting him to the crippled, powerless Hunter Zolomon

weaknesses: His own power can be turned against him: Wally unraveled his timeline
Powers came from a Cosmic Treadmill accident, not the Speed Force
unknowns: Whether his power is linked to the Speed Force is disputed among fans.
Top speed and area of effect not sourced.

sources.supports: New Earth: localized chronokinesis, alters time relative to himself rather than using the Speed Force; Wally reverts him using time-stream manipulation

DCU Guide: former FBI agent; exploded Cosmic Treadmill left him with time-related abilities
Zoom is Wally West's biggest foe; powers came from a Cosmic Treadmill accident
